glossary.definition: the branch of optics that considers the behavior of light when it exhibits wave characteristics, particularly when it interacts with small objects
$\lambda_{n} = \lambda/n$, where $\lambda$ is the wavelength in vacuum, and $n$ is the index of refraction of the medium
the bending of a wave around the edges of an opening or an obstacle
every point on a wavefront is a source of wavelets that spread out in the forward direction at the same speed as the wave itself. The new wavefront is a line tangent to all of the wavelets
waves are in phase or have a definite phase relationship

glossary.term: constructive interference for a double slit
glossary.definition: the path length difference must be an integral multiple of the wavelength

glossary.term: destructive interference for a double slit
glossary.definition: the path length difference must be a half-integral multiple of the wavelength
waves have random phase relationships
the integer $m$ used in the equations for constructive and destructive interference for a double slit

glossary.term: constructive interference for a diffraction grating
glossary.definition: occurs when the condition $d\sin\theta = m\lambda$ (for $m = 0, 1, -1, 2, -2, \ldots$) is satisfied, where $d$ is the distance between slits in the grating, $\lambda$ is the wavelength of light, and $m$ is the order of the maximum
a large number of evenly spaced parallel slits

glossary.term: destructive interference for a single slit
glossary.definition: occurs when $D\sin\theta = m\lambda$ (for $m = 1, -1, 2, -2, 3, \ldots$), where $D$ is the slit width, $\lambda$ is the light’s wavelength, $\theta$ is the angle relative to the original direction of the light, and $m$ is the order of the minimum
two images are just resolvable when the center of the diffraction pattern of one is directly over the first minimum of the diffraction pattern of the other
interference between light reflected from different surfaces of a thin film
the direction along which the filter passes the electric field of an EM wave

$\tan\theta_{\text{b}} = \frac{n_{2}}{n_{1}}$, where $n_{1}$ is the medium in which the incident and reflected light travel and $n_{2}$ is the index of refraction of the medium that forms the interface that reflects the light
